_verificationNote.authority: Rev. Proc. 2025-32, 2025-45 I.R.B., issued 2025-10-09. Section 4.01 (Tax Rate Tables, Tables 1-4) and section 4.14 (Standard Deduction). Every bracket boundary and every standard-deduction amount in this file was checked line by line against that document on 2026-08-15 and all matched.
howToRecheckAnnually: 1. The IRS inflation-adjustment revenue procedure for the tax year — for 2026 it is Rev. Proc. 2025-32: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf (index of all years: https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/inflation-adjusted-tax-items-by-tax-year)

3. Read section .01 Tax Rate Tables (Table 1 = MARRIED_JOINT, Table 2 = HEAD_OF_HOUSEHOLD, Table 3 = SINGLE, Table 4 = MARRIED_SEPARATE) and section .14 Standard Deduction. Note MARRIED_SEPARATE shares SINGLE's boundaries except the top bracket ($384,350 vs $640,600 for 2026).
_verificationNote.notModelledHere: The IRC 63(f) additional standard deduction for the aged and the blind is NOT in this file. For 2026 it is $1,650, increased to $2,050 if the individual is also unmarried and not a surviving spouse (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sec. 4.14(3)). It is separate from, and stacks with, the enhanced senior deduction in senior.2026.json, and it changes the marginal rate applied to every 65+ scenario.
